lesson_title: One Machine: the Bookkeeping Cycle, Rebuilt for the Exam
hook_text: Ten topics all year? No. It was ONE machine — and it fits in a shoebox.
clip_script: Everything you did this year in Accounting was one machine, and here it is. A shop keeps a shoebox — every slip of the month goes in: till tapes, invoices, credit notes. Step one: SORT. Six boxes, and two questions place every slip — did cash move or a promise, and which way did the value travel? Step two: each box becomes a journal, a diary of one kind of story. Step three: gather the diaries into a ledger — one page per thing, so the bank page says R8 600 in one line. Step four: the weigh-in. Every entry was a pair, debit and credit, so heap all the debits on one side of a scale and all the credits on the other — twenty thousand against twenty thousand. Level. Step five: count the street twice — the page-per-customer book against the one control line, and they must meet to the rand. Sort, write, gather, weigh, count twice. Every exam question is this machine running with different slips.
visual_style: A shoebox exploding into slips that fly into six labelled boxes; boxes stacking into a ledger shelf; a balance scale levelling at R20 000 a side; two notebooks sliding together and matching at R1 100.
pacing: Five quick machine steps, each landing on a visual click, ending on the level scale.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision session and run the machine yourself.
